title: Retry widened to timeouts under an idempotency contract; new caller posts messages
diff: -    Only ConnectionError is retried: a connection that never opened
-    cannot have had a side effect, so retrying is always safe -- the
-    decorated function does not need to be idempotent.
+    ConnectionError and TimeoutError are retried. A timed-out request
+    MAY have reached the server and taken effect before the timeout
+    fired, so decorated operations must be idempotent -- all current
+    call sites are reads or idempotent upserts.
+                    # Jitter so a fleet of workers retrying the same
"""Idempotent PUT keyed by SKU; safe to retry."""
+    """Idempotent PUT keyed by warehouse id (last-write-wins); safe
+"""Daily low-stock alerting, added for the ops channel."""
+    body = "\n".join(f"{i.sku}: {i.quantity} left" for i in items)
+        low = [i for i in stock if i.quantity <= LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD]

ground_truth.explanation: Widening RETRYABLE to include TimeoutError changes the decorator's contract, and the new docstring says so honestly: a timed-out request may already have taken effect, so decorated operations must be idempotent. The existing call sites in sync.py genuinely satisfy that (a GET and a keyed PUT). But the same diff adds low_stock_alerts.py, whose send_low_stock_alert() is a plain POST of a chat message with no idempotency key -- if the gateway accepts the message and the response times out, the retry posts it again, up to three duplicate alerts per warehouse per day. Each file is internally consistent (the decorator states its new precondition; the new module just uses the team's standard retry helper); the defect exists only in the combination, and the documented contract is one hop away from the violation.
